 De’Anthony Melton, Brandin Podziemski, Georges Niang, Yaxel Lendeborg and Charles Bassey will start Sunday’s game against the Clippers. 
 The Warriors are resting Stephen Curry and Draymond Green for Sunday’s game, prompting multiple changes to the starting lineup. Melton, Niang and Bassey will start, with Gui Santos coming off the bench after starting Friday’s win over the Lakers. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Charles Bassey 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Charles Bassey recorded 19 points (7-of-10 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), eight rebounds and one assist in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 While Bassey scored nine points in the first half, his role in the Warriors’ rotation grew more important in the second half. Draymond Green was ejected two minutes into the third quarter, giving Bassey more minutes. In 15 second-half minutes, he accumulated 10 points, six rebounds and one assist. Bassey’s 19 points are a career high, and more nights like this would go a long way toward making his contract fully guaranteed come January 10. 
 Draymond Green 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Draymond Green was ejected from Monday’s game against the Suns with 10 minutes left in the third quarter. 
 Green picked up two technical fouls early in the third quarter. After Suns center Khaman Maluach bumped him, Green got up, wrapped up Maluach, and threw him to the ground. The second technical was assessed when Green got into it with Dillon Brooks, who also received a technical foul. Green (4/4/2/1) was replaced in the lineup by Charles Bassey. 
 Gui Santos 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #15 
 Gui Santos (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Santos did not play in the second half of Sunday’s win over the Clippers, finishing with four points, three rebounds, one assist and one block in nine minutes. Following the victory, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said that the team will re-evaluate Santos, whose knee tendinitis remains an issue. At a minimum, he’ll miss Monday’s game, which could mean more playing time for Georges Niang 
 De'Anthony Melton 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #8 
 De’Anthony Melton accounted for 21 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and six three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Clippers. 
 With Stephen Curry getting the night off, Melton started Sunday’s game and played 28 minutes. Unsurprisingly, the one-time fantasy basketball darling recorded a stat line that reminded folks why he remains a popular deep-league option. Melton’s six three-pointers were the most he’s made in a game since December 9, 2022, when he hit eight as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers. With Curry expected to play Monday against the Suns, Melton will head back to the bench. 
 De'Anthony Melton 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #8 
 De’Anthony Melton produced 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Lakers. 
 Golden State’s bench made the difference on Friday, outscoring the Lakers’ bench 50-7. Melton scored 13 of his 16 points in the second quarter, shooting 3-of-4 from beyond the arc. He needed just 21 minutes to record his final stat line, showing why Melton can add value for category-league managers despite coming off the bench. The Warriors play one more game this week, hosting the Clippers on Sunday. 
 Gui Santos 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #15 
 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green will start Friday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Santos is available after sitting out Wednesday’s win over the Timberwolves and will start. His inclusion in the starting lineup comes at the expense of Georges Niang. The Warriors’ other four starters are unchanged. 
 Gui Santos 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #15 
 Gui Santos (knee) is available for Friday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Listed as doubtful on the Warriors’ initial injury report, Santos was upgraded to questionable Friday afternoon. He’s now officially available to play, which may push Georges Niang out of the starting lineup. Niang played 22 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Timberwolves. 
 Gui Santos 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #15 
 Gui Santos (knee) is doubtful to play against the Lakers on Friday. 
 Santos missed Wednesday’s game against Minnesota, which led to Georges Niang logging 22 minutes as a starter. Niang should be in line to start again but isn’t a player that’s worth streaming in any fantasy format. 
 Georges Niang 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Georges Niang, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green will start Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Gui Santos (knee) is out, opening a spot in the Warriors’ starting lineup. Niang fills the void, and he’s averaged 6.0 points per game in his first four appearances this season. 
 Yaxel Lendeborg 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Yaxel Lendeborg (foot) participated in shootaround ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Lendeborg is still listed as questionable, but this is a good sign. The rookie has been fantastic early on and should continue to put up gaudy stats, assuming he’s available for this game. If something changes, Golden State could turn to Georges Niang in the starting unit.

 Dillon Brooks amassed 18 points (5-of-8 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Brooks received a technical foul early in the third quarter that may have been more about “reputation” than anything he did in the situation that led to Draymond Green’s ejection. It isn’t a big deal right now, but the Suns getting that technical foul overturned (if they appeal it) would give Brooks a little more room later in the season. As for his performance against the Warriors, “The Villain” didn’t have any defensive stats, but the points, rebounds, assists, three-pointers and percentages were solid. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Miles Bridges accounted for 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, four steals, one block and three three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Bridges has scored at least 21 points in back-to-back games and shot the ball well on Monday. Compared to his final season with the Hornets, Bridges is averaging more rebounds, steals and blocks, while his scoring average is nearly the same (17.0 compared to 17.1 last season). Some fantasy managers may consider selling high, but Bridges’ current averages are sustainable.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Devin Booker finished Monday’s loss to the Warriors with 26 points (8-of-18 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers.
 Booker, who’s scored at least 20 points in four of Phoenix’s five games, fouled out with 57.6 seconds remaining and the Suns trailing by five. Phoenix did what it could to get one last chance to force overtime, but Collin Gillespie’s buzzer-beater attempt fell short. Booker has provided reliable fantasy value, but Phoenix’s schedule is the issue for fantasy managers. However, after playing two games in each of the first two weeks, the Suns play four games this week, counting Monday.

 Brandin Podziemski recorded 20 points (7-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 Podziemski recorded his second 20-point game of the season on Monday, finishing one point shy of his high (21 vs. the Lakers on Friday). Like Stephen Curry, Podz was most effective during the third quarter, scoring 10 points on 4-of-6 shooting from the field. The negative for fantasy managers is that Podziemski didn’t provide much value beyond the points and three-pointers. They’ll hope for more on Thursday when the Warriors host the Heat. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Stephen Curry tallied 34 points (9-of-21 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns.
 While he didn’t have his best night shooting the basketball, Curry extended his streak of games with at least 31 points to three. The Warriors star was at his best in the third quarter, shooting 6-of-9 from the field and scoring 18 points. Outside that period, the Suns kept Curry in check, but he still went home with a stat line that many fantasy managers will take without hesitation. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Player Stats

 Austin Reaves lit up the Heat with 27 points (10-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, five assists, four three-pointers and five turnovers on Monday.
 The last few games had been rough for Reaves, but he was able to get back on track in this one. The turnovers still weren’t great, and he now has 24 over his last four outings. However, he was far more efficient as a scorer, which helped the Lakers secure a second win in as many days. Reaves has been a high-level second option behind Luka Dončić this season, though the turnovers need to be cleaned up for him to match his production from last year.
 -  Noah Rubin 
 Recap 
 More Austin Reaves News
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 42 points (14-of-24 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), seven rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and six three-pointers in a 138-117 win over the Heat on Monday.
 It has been an unreal start to the season for Dončić, and Monday’s performance was just another chapter. He has scored at least 35 points and knocked down at least six three-pointers in each of his last five appearances, while going for at least 40 in four of those outings. The one game he didn’t score 40, he had 37, which was also the only game during this stretch where he shot below 50 percent from the floor. Dončić set a new season high for assists in this game as well. He has been an elite offensive engine, and he’ll look to stay hot against the Kings on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Walker Kessler 
 LAL 
 Center 
 #14 
 Player Stats

 Walker Kessler recorded a double-double on Monday with 15 points (7-of-13 FGs), 15 rebounds, two assists and two steals against the Heat.
 Kessler has finally started dominating the glass. He has recorded three straight double-doubles and has at least 15 points and 15 rebounds in each of his last two outings. Kessler has been exactly what the Lakers have needed, and it has worked out well for fantasy managers as well. With Luka Dončić running the offense, Kessler should continue to be a fantasy star.
 -  Noah Rubin

 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Player Stats

 Davion Mitchell finished with 15 points (5-of-5 FGs), seven assists, one block and four three-pointers on Monday against the Lakers.
 While Mitchell had a spectacular game, volume was an issue. He didn’t miss a shot from the floor, but he only took five shots. Mitchell has had an excellent start to the year, but his lack of shot attempts prevented him from having a better night. However, he continues to dish out the dimes at a high rate, which has been the driving factor behind his top-75 value to start this season.
 -  Noah Rubin
